items.title: Start the console with npx wingfoil-ui and have the browser open on it
items.story: As Alex, I want to start the console with `npx wingfoil-ui` and have the browser open on it, so that I use it without installing anything beyond Node 22

acceptance_criteria.title: Start the console with npx
steps: Given Node.js 22.12 is installed and no package "wingfoil-ui" is installed globally
When I run "npx wingfoil-ui"
Then the command prints a URL starting with "http://127.0.0.1:"
And the default browser opens that URL
And the page shows the project switcher with the action "Add project…"

acceptance_criteria.title: Refuse to start on an unsupported Node.js version
steps: Given Node.js 20.11 is the active Node.js version
When I run "npx wingfoil-ui"
Then the command exits with a non-zero status
And it prints "WingFoil UI needs Node.js 22.12 or later (found 20.11)"
And no port is opened

acceptance_criteria.title: Start without opening a browser when none is available
steps: Given no default browser is configured on the machine
When I run "npx wingfoil-ui"
Then the command prints the URL to open
And the server keeps running

items.title: A stable wingfoil-ui 1.0 with a published support matrix of WingFoil versions
items.story: As Alex, I want a stable `wingfoil-ui` 1.0 with a published support matrix of WingFoil versions, so that I know which of my projects it can open

acceptance_criteria.title: Install and run the stable release
steps: Given Node.js 22.12 is installed
When I run "npx wingfoil-ui@1 --version"
Then it prints "1.0.0"

acceptance_criteria.title: Publish the support matrix
steps: When I open the README of the npm package "wingfoil-ui" 1.0.0
Then its section "Supported WingFoil versions" lists the range "0.2.2 to 1.x" and, per WingFoil version, the capabilities available

acceptance_criteria.title: Pass the MVP journeys on WingFoil 1.0
steps: Given the three fixtures are built with WingFoil 1.0
When the e2e suite of every MVP story runs
Then every scenario tagged up to @v1.0 passes

acceptance_criteria.title: Print the supported range on a version mismatch
steps: Given the kanban fixture pins `wingfoil` 2.0.0
When I open the kanban fixture
Then the project header shows "WingFoil 2.0.0 — read-only: supported 0.2.2 to 1.x"

items.title: A user guide with screenshots of every MVP screen
items.story: As Riley, I want a user guide with screenshots of every MVP screen, so that I learn the console without asking the team

acceptance_criteria.title: Cover every MVP screen
steps: When I open the user guide of release 1.0.0
Then it has one section per screen: Today, element panel, Workflow, Memory, DNA, Directives, Traceability, Documentation, Team, Configuration, Timeline, Files, project switcher, command palette
And each section has at least 1 screenshot

acceptance_criteria.title: Regenerate the screenshots for the release
steps: When the screenshots of the user guide are generated for release 1.0.0
Then every screenshot is produced by the e2e suite from the fixtures at the release commit
And no screenshot file is older than that commit

acceptance_criteria.title: Pass the accessibility checks of the guide
steps: When axe-core scans every page of the user guide
Then it reports 0 violations of impact "serious" or "critical"
And every screenshot has a text alternative

items.title: The console to accept only my browser session, through a token given at launch
items.story: As a member, I want the console to accept only my browser session, through a token given at launch, so that nobody else on my machine drives my projects through it

acceptance_criteria.title: Serve the browser session opened with the token
steps: Given the console has been started with "npx wingfoil-ui" and printed its URL with the session token
And the kanban fixture is added
When I open the printed URL in the browser
Then the project switcher lists the kanban fixture
And the address bar no longer shows the token

acceptance_criteria.title: Issue a new token at every start
steps: Given the console has been started with "npx wingfoil-ui" and printed its URL with the session token
And the kanban fixture is added
Given the token printed at the previous start
When I stop the console, start it again and send an API request with the previous token
Then the response status is 401

items.title: Requests from other machines refused (loopback only)
items.story: As a member, I want requests from other machines refused (loopback only), so that nobody on my network reads or acts on my projects

acceptance_criteria.title: Listen on the loopback interface only
steps: Given the console has been started with "npx wingfoil-ui" and printed its URL with the session token
And the kanban fixture is added
When I list the server's listening sockets
Then every listening address is 127.0.0.1 or ::1

acceptance_criteria.title: Refuse a connection on the machine's network address
steps: Given the console has been started with "npx wingfoil-ui" and printed its URL with the session token
And the kanban fixture is added
Given the machine has the network address 192.0.2.10
When I send a request with the session token to "http://192.0.2.10:<port>/"
Then the connection is refused

items.title: Requests from another web page (foreign Origin or Host, DNS rebinding) or without the session token refused, writes …
items.story: As a member, I want requests from another web page (foreign Origin or Host, DNS rebinding) or without the session token refused, writes included, so that a malicious site cannot run my CLI

acceptance_criteria.title: Refuse requests without a valid session
steps: Given the console has been started with "npx wingfoil-ui" and printed its URL with the session token
And the kanban fixture is added
When I send a <method> request to the project API <condition>
Then the response status is <status>
And the server runs no `wingfoil` or `git` process for it
| method | condition                                         | status
| GET    | without the session token                         | 401
| POST   | without the session token                         | 401
| GET    | with the token and the Origin "https://evil.test" | 403
| POST   | with the token and the Origin "https://evil.test" | 403

acceptance_criteria.title: Refuse a DNS-rebinding request
steps: Given the console has been started with "npx wingfoil-ui" and printed its URL with the session token
And the kanban fixture is added
When I send a GET request with the session token and the Host header "evil.test:<port>"
Then the response status is 403

acceptance_criteria.title: Accept a request with the token from the console's own origin
steps: Given the console has been started with "npx wingfoil-ui" and printed its URL with the session token
And the kanban fixture is added
When I send a GET request with the session token, the Origin "http://127.0.0.1:<port>" and the Host "127.0.0.1:<port>"
Then the response status is 200

items.title: URLs to carry opaque project ids, never file-system paths
items.story: As a member, I want URLs to carry opaque project ids, never file-system paths, so that my folder layout is not exposed

acceptance_criteria.title: Use opaque project ids in URLs

And the kanban fixture is added
Given the kanban fixture lives at "/home/test/projects/kanban"
When I open the kanban fixture and its Memory list
Then no URL requested by the page contains "/home/test" or "projects/kanban"

acceptance_criteria.title: Refuse a project id that is not in the list
steps: Given the console has been started with "npx wingfoil-ui" and printed its URL with the session token
And the kanban fixture is added
When I send a GET request with the session token for the project id "../../etc"
Then the response status is 404

items.title: Add a project from a remote git URL, with the working directory auto-filled and the clone made for me

And the project switcher lists the project

acceptance_criteria.title: Use a working directory I typed instead of the auto-filled one

When I replace the working directory with "~/work/kanban-copy" and confirm

And "~/projects/kanban" does not exist

items.title: Reads through the CLI, direct reads on an allow-list
items.description: Governed state is read through CLI JSON output wherever the CLI exposes it (DNA, paths, workflows, Memory list and history, directive list). What the pinned CLI does not expose is read **directly, read-only, from a closed allow-list**, until WingFoil provides a read verb: `.wingfoil/memory.yaml` (type definitions: `id_pattern`, `path`, required fields, `states`), the Memory element files at the `path` given by `memory search`, and the directive files at the `path` given by `directives list`. Each directly read shape has a JSON schema in `contracts/` per supported WingFoil version, and an element's `status` read from its file must equal the one `memory search` returns (otherwise: read error). When the CLI of the project provides the read verb (capability detection), the direct read is not used. Git is read directly only for HEAD, branches, ahead/behind, working-tree status, `git log` and the working-tree files shown in Files. **Exception:** hash-only reads of the changed and untracked entries listed by `git status --porcelain`, for the repository state key (REQ-STATE-02); their content is neither kept nor exposed. The server writes none of these files.

items.title: `ui.yaml`: the UI's only file
items.description: `.wingfoil/ui.yaml` holds the UI's conventions (`version`, `taxonomy`, `progress`, `artifacts`) and nothing else — no permissions (they are WingFoil's, L6), no secrets. It has a JSON schema in `contracts/`. Without it, or when it fails the schema, the UI uses inferred defaults and warns. A preset (Kanban, Scrum, `sw-life-cycle`) is offered only when the file does not exist, refused when it maps a type the project does not declare, and validated before writing. `progress.scope` declares a type only; the current element is derived.
items.fit_criterion: [boolean] Each shipped preset validates against the schema and matches its fixture; the schema rejects a `permissions` key; every scenario listed passes.

items.title: Cache keyed on HEAD and working-tree status
items.description: Cached CLI and git reads are keyed on the commit of HEAD **and** a hash of `git status --porcelain` combined with a fingerprint of the working-tree content of each changed and untracked entry (computed by the server, no extra git command); a change of either invalidates them, so a second edit of a file that is already modified changes the state too. The effective `user.email` (repository and global git configuration) is watched too and re-evaluates the identity. Changes are detected by file watching, with a periodic check as a fallback.

items.title: Progress scope and computations
items.description: Completion and iterated figures cover the current element of the `progress.scope` type: with WingFoil 0.3 the one `workflow status` reports; before it, the most advanced element not in its first or last non-archived state (ties: lowest version); none → whole project. Reference completion = done linked elements / linked elements; project completion = unweighted mean over references with ≥ 1 linked element (Q8); coverage = elements carrying all `requires` categories / elements whose type has `requires`, project-wide. Open bugs and pending gates are project-wide; a state both gate and `waiting:` is not a pending gate.

items.title: Git interface
items.description: The server runs only these git operations: read (`rev-parse`, `status --porcelain`, `log`, `rev-list --count`, `config user.email`, `remote`), `clone` (adding a remote project, into a new empty folder), `fetch`, `pull --ff-only`, `push`, and `add -- .wingfoil/ui.yaml` + `commit -- .wingfoil/ui.yaml` for presets. It never merges, rebases, resets, stashes or checks out. Git's error message is shown verbatim on failure. Memory events (Timeline, Recent activity) are parsed from `wf(…)` subjects; `add` and `submit` subjects carry no transition, so a submit's `from → to` is read from the element file's `status` before and after the commit (project-wide views: one `git log -p` over the Memory directories; element panel: `memory history <id>`, which carries the states — `spec-002-memory-events-from-git`).
items.fit_criterion: [percentage] 100 % of the git processes started during the e2e suite use a subcommand of the allowed list (process audit).

items.title: Session token
items.description: Each start issues a new random session token (≥ 128 bits), given in the printed URL's fragment, removed from the address bar after the first load and exchanged for a browser session; the token or that session is required on every API request and on the event stream — the static application files, which hold no project data, are exempt. Neither is ever written to logs or disk.
items.fit_criterion: [percentage] 100 % of API and event-stream requests without the current token or a session derived from it (or with a previous start's) get HTTP 401 and start 0 processes; the token and the session id appear in 0 log lines.
